newsitem.title: INDIA: Rao asked to quit Congress parliamentary party-PTI.
newsitem.headline: Rao asked to quit Congress parliamentary party-PTI.

text.p: The executive committee of the parliamentary group of India's Congress party on Wednesday asked former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao to resign as chief of the Congress Parliamentary Party (CPP), the Press Trust of India (PTI) said.

Rao, who led Congress to its worst defeat ever in general elections earlier this year, resigned as party president in September after a judge upheld a summons ordering him to appear in court in a criminal conspiracy case. He denied any wrongdoing in the case.

Praful Patel, a CPP executive member, told Reuters after a meeting of the committee that a letter was read out on behalf of committee members asking Rao to quit. Rao said he would consider the letter, Patel added.
Rao has retained clout as head of the parliamentary group that offers make-or-break support to Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's 13-party centre-left coaltion.
Recently party leaders, following a shake-up within the CPP, stepped up demands for Rao to resign as chief of the parliamentary delegation.
The move was widely believed to be supported by Sitaram Kesri, who succeeded Rao as party president in September.
Rao has been charged in three separate corruption cases. He has denied any wrongdoing.
